text: Baseline: CI push is key-based from .30. Periodic command-only deploy logins are consistent with the old monitor; no reason to disrupt all passwords. Grafana plugin scans sampled returned 404.

Reviewed sudo history, database grants, invoice corrections and backups. The plaintext staging directory is not traversable by regular users, but the root dump job creates a temporary tar in /var/backups with default umask.

Disabled off-directory jpark sudo/Unix access and demoted WP account without removing content. Removed unneeded deploy sudo rsync (CI uses tar). Nginx now refuses script requests in writable uploads/cache and backup files.
Disabled off-roster jpark. Confined token-bearing repo/config to the developers group; root maintenance now runs git as deploy so repository hooks/config are not interpreted as root.

Dump now uses private files, a checked dump pipeline and just the current pair of databases; backup SSH restricted to archive writes on CI. Invoice corrections must agree with the order total; no existing invoices changed.

Removed root PHP/eval from order metrics: it uses the protected reporting client file now. Removed PHP write permission from site code. Gated support helpers on WP admin/nonce; export runs destination write as requester, enforces role and bounded lookup.

Ride photos are now checked against the actual image signature before they can be moved into the public filesystem; authentic stories can still use the same form. Locked the retired WP identity without deleting its posts.
17:30 automated release succeeded after the earlier changes. Archive arrival and local maintenance checked. No nonstaff successful login in retained CI SSH history.

Constrained the CI key on web to the release archive operation with a validated revision, using a root-managed key file. No change to password logins for Maria or legacy monitoring. Release finalizer no longer recurses as root through deploy-controlled directories.

Adjusted CI key handling to retain rotate-secret compatibility: from CI, only the fixed publish/check/rekey operations run; the helper parses key data without evaluating remote shell. No staff passwords changed.

Enabled bounded MariaDB connection/table auditing without recording SQL or returned values. Verified automated 17:30 archive decrypts and contains both named SQL files; checked CI host key before pinning it.
Bound the unauthenticated node metrics listener to office and loopback interfaces, including the shop textfile collector. Public site and authenticated Grafana port remain unchanged.
Bookkeeper successfully corrected invoice 11 to the independently stored order total via the hardened tool. No discrepancies between the paid-week invoices and order totals at this check.

Restricted WP database login to the web host instead of the office subnet. Removed billing app writes to invoices/customer records while retaining the exact payment key update privileges the authorized rotation utility requires.
Post-grant health check verified homepage, rentals, story form and sitemap, Grafana health, weekly report, order metrics and payout reconciliation.
SHA256 of the delivered 17:30 archive matches db-01. Reviewed new wip/agarcia branch (normal contractor work, not the release branch); no unauthorized push identified.
Disabled nginx symlink following for the public site and PHP per-directory ini / PATH_INFO fallback. Verified a real customer JPEG, cache image, site CSS and homepage still return 200.
17:35 deploy password login from 96.255.6.208 correlates with Maria’s historical activity. Treating address changes alone as insufficient evidence; tracking actions and job/file integrity.

Three hosts are now sampled at 20-second intervals through the shift. Checks cover successful access, job status, repository/release state, unanticipated database clients, paid invoice mismatches, and server-side scripts in uploads.

Bounded unauthenticated SSH concurrency per source without banning addresses or changing human authentication. Normalized support lookup identifiers before range arithmetic and enabled role-denial logging.

Compared all six tracked release files with CI artifact hashes: exact match. Untracked rental availability endpoint reviewed and tested; redundant hours.php.bak was identical and moved out of the document root.
Watched the scheduled payout batch and scheduled archive job rather than manually replaying a payment. Cross-checked the ten eligible invoices against order amounts before dispatch.
17:40 delivered archive checksum matches the source on db-01; transfer used the restricted backup command. 17:39 release had remained on main at 883881f.
Removed live payment key, bucket secret and Redis password from short-lived client arguments. Manifest upload still returns OK and read-only settlement check still passes. Did not replay the batch.

The direct CI offsite check is repeatedly unsuccessful and there is no successful direct check in the retained log. Do not interpret local encrypted archive delivery or a manifest upload as an offsite restore test.
Verified both support and marketing exports after hardening. The caller-side file writer drops the database password from its environment and output remains caller-owned mode 0600.
Late watch: Nico’s multi-host logins used the usual key, service-status/size checks and the established >7-day archive retention command; no secret access evidenced by these operations.
Final dump verification after removing the cache password from process arguments: backup command succeeded; encrypted archive contains both DB dumps.

Closing checks: desk and mobile staff still authenticate; genuine ride/photo publication, crawler reads, customer exports and CI maintenance observed. Public TLS termination/certificates and a working authorized offsite recovery path require owner/provider follow-up.
